text:
GENERATE BURST CS-vfx-bwc-sheets-v2 — greyscale PAINTED-PIXEL effect sheets for BLACKWATER COCKTAIL (breadth test kit 2: gd-bwc-demolitionist; style card v0.2). task_id "CS-vfx-bwc-sheets-v2".

Paint ONE 1536×1024 image on flat PURE BLACK #000000 — the background is a BLACK VOID: NO grey fog, NO gradient, NO vignette, NO atmosphere, NO lighting on the background; every background pixel is exactly #000000 (this is the one hard rule; a grey or hazy background is a failed image). The flask glass is drawn MID GREY so it stays visible against black. a 6-column × 4-row grid of 256×256 cells (each effect drawing centred in its cell, never touching the cell edge), GREYSCALE ONLY (light grey → mid grey → dark grey → darker grey (use pure WHITE only for the tiniest fuse spark and the very centre of the flame cores, never for whole shapes), no colour), in a PAINTED-PIXEL register: each drawing looks like a hand-painted sprite at a small native size — hard-edged shapes, 3–4 flat value steps, a near-white core, dark grey rim/interior holes, ABSOLUTELY NO soft gradients, NO glow, NO haze, NO bloom, NO radial light falloff around any shape, NO blur, NO anti-aliasing, NO outline strokes: every pixel is one of exactly FIVE values — pure black background, dark grey #404040, mid grey #808080, light grey #C0C0C0, pure white #FFFFFF — with hard, stair-stepped edges as if drawn with a 1-px pencil at 64 px and scaled up 4x with nearest-neighbour. Think 1990s 16-bit sprite effects (Diablo I / Secret of Mana spell sprites) drawn in greyscale, NOT a modern glowing render. If you are tempted to make anything glow, draw a ring of light-grey pixels instead. Design it as a thrown burning-oil flask effect (glass flask, oil splash, oily fire tongues, black smoke puffs, burning pool) even though it is greyscale.
ROW 1 — CAST (6 frames, left to right in time): a small round flask appears in a hand-sized swing arc, lit by a tiny fuse spark growing brighter; frame 6 the flask is released, tilted, fuse flaring.
ROW 2 — TRAVEL (6 frames): the flask tumbling in flight drawn facing RIGHT: a rotating flask silhouette with a short fuse-spark trail to the LEFT; each frame a different rotation so they loop.
ROW 3 — IMPACT (6 frames): the flask shatters: frame 1 a low flat splash of oil with glass shards (NO white disc — the palest grey is the brightest value); then fire tongues erupt low and wide from the splash; then a broader burst of oily flames with a few black smoke puffs; the last frame is thinning flame tongues and smoke.
ROW 4 — RESIDUAL + EMBER (6 frames): frames 1–4: a wide flat burning pool on the ground (an ellipse wider than tall, low fire tongues along its rim) in four looping variations of the same size; frames 5–6: one single small ember/oil-drop spark facing RIGHT, two variants.
Every drawing must read at 25 % size (64 px cells). Nothing between cells; no labels, grid lines, text or border; background pure black.

One image_gen call. ONE retry only if colour appears, any glow/haze/gradient appears, cells bleed into each other, or a row is missing — name the reason. Copy the output from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/... to out/bwc_sheets_v2.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "CS-vfx-bwc-sheets-v2"; images = the file with prompt, references and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.
